comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 53-page OER Appendix 3, printed pp.34–36, explicitly applies the renewed programme to students starting in 2025–2026. English first-year study and the neutrally selected International Economics and Policy route supply 180 documented EC. Article 17 permits approved, non-overlapping university study in the 24-EC choice space; this is not an unrestricted guarantee. Appendix 4, printed p.39, retains Academic Skills and OIM-A/MRI plus statistics entry requirements for the thesis, without an explicit renewed-course equivalence. No 2026-entry future-year programme, waiver or formal thesis eligibility is certified.

core: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, international markets, strategic choices and empirical economic explanation
Mathematics, statistics, data analysis, applied econometrics and independent economic research
Business economics, accounting, corporate finance and organisational strategy
Economic policy, inequality and the consequences of decisions for society and sustainability
adjacent: Financial markets, risk and behavioural financial decisions
Accounting and financial reporting as a specialised route
Sustainability, responsible firms and distributive consequences of economic policy
questions: How can economic policy respond to global sustainability challenges and unequal outcomes?
How can businesses remain financially viable while accounting for environmental and social responsibilities?

alternatives.label: Economics, business & quantitative policy
alternatives.concept: A programme linking microeconomics, macroeconomics, public and behavioural economics with econometrics, accounting, finance and business decisions. Climate, governance and political institutions provide specific complements to economic-policy inquiry; specialist economics depth and a required economics thesis are not reproduced.
progression: All six covered terms and formal earlier prerequisites checked against the current workbook. Relevant foundations precede advanced dependents where feasible; the external thesis-entry uncertainty is separately disclosed.

alternatives.label: Economic policy, responsible business and sustainability
alternatives.concept: A programme asking how governments and businesses respond to climate pressures and unequal outcomes. It retains economic theory, accounting, statistics and econometrics, while adding environmental governance, political institutions, social inequality and commercial law.
alternatives.labelReason: The final course set combines eight economics/business courses with policy, social inequality, climate and governance; its label identifies that real combination rather than calling it a sustainability-specialist economics degree.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad route, five actual substitutions replace specialist banking, mathematical statistics, consumer marketing and organisational psychology with commercial regulation, environmental foundations, international politics and social/environmental justice. These choices serve the evidenced policy and responsible-business question, not numerical variety.
progression: All six covered terms and formal earlier prerequisites checked against the current workbook. Relevant foundations precede advanced dependents where feasible; the external thesis-entry uncertainty is separately disclosed.

candidates.label: Economic policy, responsible business and sustainability
Finance and financial market stability
candidates.reason: Money, Banking & Finance supplies asset pricing, risk, regulation and a bank simulation; Accounting adds investment appraisal. Both are already in the closest programme. These real contributions do not supply a sustained distinct 24-course finance route with further specialist investment and risk study.

candidates.label: Accounting and financial reporting
candidates.reason: The current UCR workbook has one accounting and corporate finance course but no advanced financial reporting, management accounting, auditing or control sequence to anchor a separate 24-course accounting route.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target contains three current specialisations. International Economics and Policy covers economic theory, international markets, sustainability, inequality and policy and therefore best represents the degree’s broad academic economics identity. Accounting and Finance are more sector-specific; this choice was made from Radboud’s stated programme, independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

blocks: Economic theory, markets and empirical questions
Both introduce micro and macroeconomic analysis; UCR compresses the range into one course.
Both analyse inflation, growth and macroeconomic policy; UCR approaches these internationally.
Both address consumer choice, markets and strategic behaviour, though UCR is an advanced course.
Both study experimental and behavioural explanations of economic decisions.
Both analyse public spending, market failure and the economics of policy.
No included UCR course directly treats development economics as an economic subfield.
Sociology and public economics touch inequality but do not directly teach labour economics.
General market strategy and behavioural economics do not replace a dedicated game-theory course.
Modern history and business study do not directly teach the disciplinary history of economic thought.
Both teach statistics and basic empirical methods; Radboud embeds these in an economics curriculum.
Both build mathematical techniques used in economic analysis; UCR includes applications beyond economics.
Both estimate economic relationships with econometric methods; UCR does not provide Radboud’s two-stage sequence.
UCR has one econometrics course aligned to the first applied sequence; no separately credited second stage appears.
The UCR data workflow supports empirical inquiry but does not establish this dedicated applied economics-and-policy methods course.
Both introduce firm choices and business planning; UCR is more venture-centred and lacks the full finance scope.
Both analyse corporate financial statements and accounting information; UCR is less specialised.
Both introduce marketing strategy and consumer engagement; UCR develops it as a later elective.
Both examine firm strategy in changing markets; UCR emphasises digital transformation.

Partial international-economics relationship through actual trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and monetary-system analysis. UCR applies these to firms and market-entry decisions rather than the full economic-theory course.
The UCR banking/finance course does not separately reproduce international financial policy.
UCR accounting includes investment appraisal and occupies the accounting row. Banking and asset pricing do not reproduce a full corporate investment and financing course.
UCR studies environmental governance and impacts, but no scheduled course directly teaches the economics of sustainability at Radboud’s scope.
No single scheduled course covers the advanced topical seminar in international economics and policy as such.
Personal development, specialist electives and thesis
Both develop academic and professional reflection, though UCR personal development has a different focus.
24 EC of approved university-level choice, subject to non-overlap and applicable approval conditions.
Radboud requires a twelve-credit economics thesis; UCR independent research appears only as a comparison-only option.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated multi-year economics and business-economics curriculum with a named specialisation, staged econometrics and a required economics thesis. UCR combines its economics, business, quantitative, policy and sustainability courses flexibly, but these programmes do not reproduce Radboud’s disciplinary depth or mandatory thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught degree studies economic choices, markets, firms and their social consequences. It combines microeconomics, macroeconomics, accounting, finance and quantitative research, followed here through International Economics and Policy. The illustrated renewed curriculum is for students who entered in 2025–2026.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed economics and business-economics curriculum supports two meaningful UCR responses: quantitative economics/business study and economic policy with responsible business and sustainability. UCR offers less specialist economics, finance and accounting depth and does not reproduce the staged econometrics sequence or required economics thesis. The unresolved thesis-entry rules prevent certification of the external pathway.

curriculum.limitation: The published components total 180 EC. The current thesis-entry table uses earlier methods-course names that have not been formally reconciled with the renewed curriculum. Thesis eligibility and old/new course equivalence are not verified.

componentNotes.y3-electives: 24 EC of approved choice, subject to university-level study, non-overlap and applicable approval conditions.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The 12-EC economics thesis is documented; eligibility under the renewed curriculum remains unverified.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 26 published positions for the renewed 2025–2026 entrant cohort, totalling 180 EC, including 24 EC of approved choice and a 12-EC economics thesis.
comparisonScope.excluded: Certification of thesis eligibility, earlier/new methods-course equivalence, waivers and a complete formally verified external progression pathway.

acceptance.claim: The confirmed economics and business-economics curriculum supports two meaningful UCR responses: quantitative economics/business study and economic policy with responsible business and sustainability.
acceptance.targetContext: CP041: English-taught Radboud Economics and Business Economics; 2026–2027 adopted OER; explicitly illustrated 2025–2026 entrant cohort; International Economics and Policy selected for broad academic identity.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified source-first second pass by the same AI reviewer against the official OER, current UCR evidence and exact finished inputs; no independent human or separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: The published components total 180 EC. The current thesis-entry table uses earlier methods-course names that have not been formally reconciled with the renewed curriculum. Thesis eligibility and old/new course equivalence are not verified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The renewed methods courses are formally recognized as satisfying the older entry names.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The academic subjects and both UCR responses remain; this formal equivalence is not assumed.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Additional preparation, substitution or a different thesis-entry sequence is required.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Formal eligibility changes. The verified theory, methods, firms and policy inquiry remains substantial and the limited UCR academic response survives. No extra preparation or waiver is inserted into the 180 EC.
